The clue is the next verse: 'predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers' (Rom 8:29); and 'Abba, Father' stands at 8:15.

**This is a call the compiler had to make.** The verse says *God*. It is pointed at the Father as well because the verse or its neighbour puts God in a father-relation -- his Son, his only begotten, the Father -- and not merely in the same sentence as Jesus. Where no such clue is near, the saying stays on God alone; 'God does not show favoritism' (Acts 10:34) is the worked example of the rule declining. Readers who take God and the Father to be one record throughout will find the extra edge redundant rather than wrong; readers who do not can drop it, because it is marked.
